description: An introduction to Salah covering its importance, the five daily prayers and their rakaa, the conditions, pillars and nullifiers of prayer, congregational prayer and the times of prayer.

mcq.questionText: How many obligatory (fardh) prayers must a Muslim perform each day and night?
mcq.explanation: Islam obligates five daily prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the prayer performed before sunrise?
mcq.explanation: Fajr is the dawn prayer, performed after dawn appears but before sunrise.

mcq.questionText: How many rakaa does the Fajr prayer contain?
mcq.explanation: Fajr is the shortest obligatory prayer, consisting of two rakaa.

mcq.questionText: Which prayer consists of three rakaa?
mcq.explanation: Maghrib, the prayer after sunset, is the only obligatory prayer with three rakaa.

mcq.questionText: How many rakaa are there in the Dhuhr prayer?
mcq.explanation: Dhuhr, the midday prayer, contains four rakaa.

mcq.questionText: What is the purification with water required before prayer called?
mcq.explanation: Wudhu (ablution) is the act of washing certain body parts with water and is a condition for valid prayer.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is one of the conditions (shuruut) that must be met before Salah is valid?
mcq.explanation: Facing the Qiblah (direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah) is a condition for the validity of Salah.

mcq.questionText: Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah is considered what part of the prayer?
mcq.explanation: Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar (rukn) of the prayer in each rakaa, without which the prayer is incomplete.

mcq.questionText: What is the opening phrase 'Allahu Akbar' that begins the prayer called?
mcq.explanation: Takbiratul-Ihram is the saying of 'Allahu Akbar' that marks the start of the prayer and is a pillar of Salah.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following actions nullifies (breaks) the Salah?

options.text: Eating or drinking deliberately during prayer
Saying the tasleem at the end

mcq.explanation: Eating or drinking intentionally during the prayer invalidates it.

mcq.questionText: The call that summons Muslims to come and perform the prayer is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The Adhan is the call to prayer announced by the mu'adhin at the entry of each prayer time.

mcq.questionText: Praying together in a group behind a leader is called:
mcq.explanation: Congregational prayer (salatul-jama'ah) is prayer performed in a group following an imam and carries greater reward.

mcq.questionText: The person who leads the congregational prayer is called the:
mcq.explanation: The Imam stands in front and leads the congregation, who follow his movements in prayer.

mcq.questionText: Which prayer time begins immediately after the sun sets?
mcq.explanation: Maghrib begins right after the sun has fully set and lasts until the red twilight disappears.

mcq.questionText: Why is Salah important in the life of a Muslim?

options.text: It is only a cultural tradition
It is the second pillar of Islam and a direct link between a servant and Allah
It is performed only during Ramadhan
It replaces the need for fasting

mcq.explanation: Salah is the second pillar of Islam, a daily act of worship that connects the believer with Allah and will be the first deed judged on the Day of Judgement.

fib.questionText: The prayer performed in the middle of the afternoon is called _____.
fib.explanation: Asr is the afternoon prayer, performed after Dhuhr and before sunset, and contains four rakaa.

fib.questionText: The night prayer, which is the last of the five daily prayers, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Isha is the night prayer, consisting of four rakaa.

fib.questionText: Both the Asr and the Isha prayers consist of _____ rakaa each.
fib.explanation: Asr, Dhuhr and Isha each have four obligatory rakaa.

fib.questionText: The act of washing specific body parts with water to be ready for prayer is called _____.
fib.explanation: Wudhu is the ritual ablution and a prerequisite for the validity of Salah.

fib.questionText: When water is unavailable or harmful, a Muslim may purify himself using clean earth in an act called _____.
fib.explanation: Tayammum is dry ablution using clean earth, permitted when water cannot be used.

fib.questionText: Muslims face the direction of the Ka'bah during prayer, which is known as the _____.
fib.explanation: The Qiblah is the direction towards the Ka'bah in Makkah that all Muslims face when praying.

fib.questionText: The bowing position in prayer, in which the back is bent and hands placed on the knees, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Rukoo is the bowing pillar of the prayer performed after recitation.

fib.questionText: Placing the forehead on the ground in worship is called _____.
fib.explanation: Sujood (prostration) is a pillar of Salah in which the forehead, nose, palms, knees and toes touch the ground.

fib.questionText: The prayer is ended by turning the head and saying the greeting of peace, known as the _____.
fib.explanation: The tasleem is the final pillar, saying 'Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullah' to the right and left.

fib.questionText: Speaking unnecessary words to another person during prayer will _____ the Salah.
fib.explanation: Deliberately speaking to people during the prayer is one of the things that nullify (break) Salah.

tf.questionText: Salah is the second pillar of Islam.
tf.explanation: After the declaration of faith (Shahadah), Salah is the second of the five pillars of Islam.

tf.questionText: There are six obligatory daily prayers in Islam.
tf.explanation: There are five obligatory daily prayers, not six: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

tf.questionText: The Maghrib prayer has three rakaa.
tf.explanation: Maghrib is the only obligatory prayer with three rakaa.

tf.questionText: A Muslim may pray without first covering the parts of the body that must be covered (awrah).
tf.explanation: Covering the awrah is a condition for valid prayer, so the prayer is not valid without it.

tf.questionText: Facing the Qiblah is one of the conditions for a valid prayer.
tf.explanation: Facing the Qiblah (the direction of the Ka'bah) is a required condition of Salah.

tf.questionText: Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah is a pillar of the prayer.
tf.explanation: Al-Fatihah must be recited in each rakaa and is a pillar (rukn) of Salah.

tf.questionText: Laughing out loud during prayer does not affect the validity of the Salah.
tf.explanation: Laughing out loud during prayer is among the things that nullify the Salah.

tf.questionText: Praying in congregation carries greater reward than praying alone.
tf.explanation: The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that congregational prayer is many times more rewarding than praying individually.

tf.questionText: Each prayer has its own fixed time during which it must be performed.
tf.explanation: Salah is prescribed at specific times, and performing it within its appointed time is a condition of its validity.

tf.questionText: Tayammum can be performed using clean earth when water is not available.
tf.explanation: Tayammum is the permitted dry purification using clean earth when water is unavailable or cannot be used.

summary.explanation: They are Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
Fajr is the dawn prayer with two rakaa.
Maghrib is the only obligatory prayer with three rakaa.

summary.questionText: Rakaa of Dhuhr, Asr and Isha
summary.explanation: Each of these three prayers contains four obligatory rakaa.
Tayammum with clean earth replaces wudhu when water is unavailable.
Muslims face the Ka'bah in Makkah during Salah.

summary.explanation: These are essential acts without which the prayer is invalid.

summary.questionText: Examples of things that nullify Salah
summary.correctAnswer: Eating, drinking, speaking deliberately, and laughing out loud
summary.explanation: These actions break the prayer and require it to be repeated.
The congregation follows the Imam's movements in the prayer.

summary.explanation: It is the first deed to be judged on the Day of Judgement.

hoq.questionText: If a person begins praying Asr but realises midway that he never performed wudhu, what is the correct ruling regarding his prayer?

options.text: The prayer is valid because he had good intention
The prayer is invalid because wudhu is a condition that must exist before the prayer
He may continue and perform wudhu after finishing
He only needs to repeat the last rakaa

hoq.explanation: Wudhu is a condition (shart) that must be fulfilled before the prayer begins; without it the entire prayer is invalid and must be repeated after performing wudhu.

hoq.questionText: A latecomer joins the congregation while the Imam is already in rukoo of the second rakaa. Why does the order of pillars matter for how he completes his prayer?

options.text: Because the pillars of Salah must be performed in their proper sequence
Because he can skip any pillars he missed
Because congregational prayer has no pillars
Because the Imam performs the pillars on his behalf entirely

hoq.explanation: The pillars (arkan) of Salah must be done in order, so after the Imam finishes the latecomer must stand and make up the rakaa he missed, performing each pillar in its correct sequence.

hoq.questionText: Two prayers are alike in having four rakaa, yet one is recited aloud and the other silently. Which pairing correctly contrasts an aloud (jahri) four-rakaa prayer with a silent (sirri) one?

options.text: Isha is recited aloud while Dhuhr is recited silently
Asr is recited aloud while Isha is recited silently
Dhuhr is recited aloud while Isha is recited silently
Both Dhuhr and Asr are recited aloud

hoq.explanation: Among the four-rakaa prayers, Isha has its first two rakaa recited aloud, whereas Dhuhr and Asr are recited silently throughout.
